title: The Mole and Molar Mass
seo_title: Mole Worksheets: Molar Mass, Grams to Moles and Avogadro's Number (High School Chemistry)
standard_text: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on the mole (NGSS HS-PS1-7): molar mass, grams to moles, moles to particles with Avogadro's number and percent composition. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Molar mass turns grams into moles, and moles into particles.
body_html:
How to think about it

The mole links counting to weighing.

  • 1 mol = 6.02 × 1023 particles. Molar mass (g/mol) = sum of the atomic masses in the formula.
  • grams ÷ molar mass = moles; moles × molar mass = grams; moles × 6.02 × 1023 = particles.
  • Subscripts tell how many moles of each atom are in one mole of the compound.
Example

Molar mass of H2O (H = 1, O = 16)?

2 × 1 + 16

Answer: 18 g/mol

Example

Moles in 36 g of water?

36 ÷ 18

Answer: 2 mol

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying by molar mass when changing grams to moles.
  • Forgetting a subscript when adding atomic masses.
  • Thinking 1 mol of a compound has 1 mol of atoms.

faq.q: How do you find molar mass?
faq.a: Add the atomic masses of all the atoms in the formula, multiplying each by its subscript. For H₂O: 2 × 1 + 16 = 18 g/mol.

faq.q: How do you convert grams to moles?
faq.a: Divide the mass in grams by the molar mass in g/mol.
6.02 × 10²³, the number of particles in one mole of a substance.

items.q: What is the molar mass of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>)? (C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)
One mole of carbon (12 g) and one mole of oxygen gas (32 g) have the same what?
Why do chemists use moles?
c: Grams do not exist in chemistry.
Atoms are too small to count one by one, so moles link counts to masses we can weigh.
